blocks.text: Jeremiah 23 does not treat a prophetic claim as self-authenticating. The chapter contrasts prophets who promise peace with the claim that they were not sent and did not stand in Jehovah’s council. A disputed contextual reading connects this issue with the wider conflict between Jeremiah and Hananiah, where yokes, peace, timing, and outcomes were contested. The chapter’s repeated questions—“What hath Jehovah answered?” and “What hath Jehovah spoken?”—therefore press the issue of how competing claims to speak for Jehovah are to be weighed.

Jeremiah 23 belongs to a received book that combines poetic material, prose sermons, narratives, letters, headings, repeated accounts, restoration collections, oracles concerning nations, and an appendix. A practical outline places chapters 2–25 together before later collections and narratives, while leaving questions about the book’s long compositional and textual history unsettled. This helps situate the chapter within a larger, varied book rather than treating every section as the same kind of writing.
